Carajillo con Mantilla

This Carajillo was easily one of the best carajillos I’ve EVER had.
Made with Stone Groove Bourbon, Spanish vanilla, Portola Coffee, and orange bitters, it was already a fantastic cocktail. Then it was finished with a delicate piece of honeycomb that you eat with the drink, turning it into more than just a cocktail. It became an experience.

I’m honestly disappointed that I didn’t get better photos of this one because it absolutely deserved it.

Looks like I have another reason to head back to Stone Groove Stillhouse. Next time, I’m bringing more camera gear and spending a lot more time photographing this drink.

caption: One of the things that intrigued me most about Stone Groove Stillhouse wasn’t just the cocktails. It was the idea behind the spirits themselves.
fullCaption:
One of the things that intrigued me most about Stone Groove Stillhouse wasn’t just the cocktails. It was the idea behind the spirits themselves.

They’ve developed a process they call Musically Mastered™, where spirits mature in an environment influenced by music, sound, vibration, and resonance. The idea is that different genres create different energy during the aging process, ultimately influencing how the spirit develops.

I’ll be honest… I can’t pretend to understand exactly how music changes the taste of a spirit.

What I can say is that every cocktail I had was incredible. Whether it was the spirits themselves, the bartenders, or a combination of both, something is clearly working.

It’s one of the most unique concepts I’ve come across, and as someone who appreciates both music and craftsmanship, I love seeing people experiment with ideas like this instead of doing what everyone else is doing.

Now I just need to go back and do one of their spirit tastings because I’m genuinely curious to experience the differences for myself.

Have you ever tried a spirit that’s been aged or crafted in a completely unique way?

caption: One of my favorite things about photography is that it gives me an excuse to explore places I probably would’ve overlooked otherwise.
fullCaption:
One of my favorite things about photography is that it gives me an excuse to explore places I probably would’ve overlooked otherwise.

I’ve lived in Anaheim for years, and somehow it took me way too long to finally check out Stone Groove Stillhouse inside Anaheim MAKE. That was mistake number one.

Mistake number two? Showing up with only my Sony a7CR and a Viltrox 85mm f/2.

The lens did a great job for tighter shots, but this place deserves more than one perspective. Between the lighting, the cocktails, and all the little details throughout the space, I already know I need to come back with a wider lens and a flash.

Stone Groove Stillhouse is billed as the world’s first Audio Stillhouse and a HiFi cocktail bar, and after spending an evening there, I completely understand why people keep talking about it. The food, the drinks, the atmosphere, and especially the staff made the experience even better.

Huge thanks to the entire team for being so welcoming and accommodating while I wandered around taking photos. I already can’t wait to come back, and next time I’m bringing more gear and a few more friends.

Have you been to Stone Groove Stillhouse yet, or is this your first time hearing about it?

caption: This is exactly why I started Capture Create Caffeinate.
fullCaption:
This is exactly why I started Capture Create Caffeinate.

I love discovering local businesses with great food, great drinks, and an atmosphere that makes me want to pull my camera out. If I can build this page around supporting places like that while continuing to improve as a photographer and filmmaker, I’ll consider that a win.

Stone Groove Stillhouse has honestly become one of my favorite places in Anaheim. Between the HiFi concept, the cocktails, the lighting, and the overall atmosphere, it feels like it was made to be photographed and filmed. I already have a friend I want to bring here because I know they’ll love it as much as I did.

This video is really just a proof of concept.

When I visited, I wasn’t planning on shooting video. I had no idea I was walking into a place this beautiful, so I wasn’t carrying the gear I normally would’ve brought. Looking back, I already know exactly how I’d approach it differently. Better lenses, better camera movement, more intentional lighting, and a stronger story.

That just gives me another reason to come back.

I’d love to make this a regular part of Capture Create Caffeinate: discovering local spots, telling their stories through photos and video, and hopefully introducing more people to businesses that deserve the attention.

I’d love to hear what you think of this style of content. And if you’ve been to Stone Groove Stillhouse before, let me know what keeps bringing you back.

caption: As someone who doesn’t drink beer, finding a spot that serves great cider means I am definitely going back. Unsung Brewing at Anaheim Make is exactly that place.
I found a spot I didn’t even know existed until recently, and I’m definitely going back.
fullCaption:
I found a spot I didn’t even know existed until recently, and I’m definitely going back.

Unsung Brewing at Anaheim Make near the Anaheim Packing District is one of those places that just feels comfortable the moment you walk in. It has a nerdy, comic-book inspired vibe that immediately feels like home if you’re into that kind of culture.

I don’t really drink beer, but I do like cider, and they had options that made it easy for me to actually enjoy being there without feeling like I had to force anything.

What stood out most was the atmosphere. It’s relaxed, creative, and full of little details that make the space interesting without trying too hard.

While I was there, I even saw people doing Disney pin trading, which honestly makes sense given how close it is to Disneyland. It feels like a spot where Disney fans, locals, and creatives naturally overlap.

If you haven’t been to Anaheim Make near the Anaheim Packing District, this is one of those places worth checking out. I’ll definitely be making this a regular stop.
